fine_trace.note: InflateRankDims decompresses the attacker-controlled zlib stream into the fixed 16-element stack array uncomp_buf. The crafted stream emits only 6 of the 8 dims-tag bytes (miINT32 type + the low two bytes 0x0AD8 of the size field) and then ends, so inflate returns Z_STREAM_END and InflateRankDims returns early without allocating a heap dims buffer, leaving *dims NULL.

Because InflateRankDims returned early (*dims == NULL), the caller falls back to aliasing dims to the stack array uncomp_buf + 2, so the subsequent copy loop reads the dimension words from the fixed 16-element stack buffer.

nbytes is taken from the attacker-controlled decompressed dims-tag size field; only the low two bytes (0xD8 0x0A) were written by the stream, the high bytes are stale zeros from the {0,} initialization, yielding nbytes = 0x00000AD8 = 2776.

matvar->rank is derived from the attacker-controlled byte count (2776/4 = 694) with no validation that it fits in the remaining entries of the 16-element uncomp_buf when dims aliases uncomp_buf+2; the missing guard is rank <= 13 (the fix adds: if (0 == do_clean && matvar->rank > 13) { error; break; }).
The destination array is heap-allocated with matvar->rank (694) elements; the allocation succeeds, so the copy loop below executes for j = 0 .. 693.

The copy loop reads dims[j] = uncomp_buf[2+j]; for j >= 14 (rank > 13) the read goes past the 16-element uncomp_buf stack array, the first out-of-bounds access being dims[14] = uncomp_buf[16], which ASan reports as a 4-byte stack-buffer-overflow READ at this line.

via: dims[j] read in the copy loop

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: The PoC is a compressed (zlib) MAT v5 file whose decompressed stream emits the miMATRIX variable tag, the array flags, and only the first 6 bytes of the dims tag (miINT32 type followed by the low two bytes 0x0AD8 of the size field) before the zlib stream ends. InflateRankDims therefore returns early on Z_STREAM_END leaving *dims NULL, the caller falls back to dims = uncomp_buf + 2, and the attacker-controlled rank (2776/4 = 694 > 13) drives the copy loop to read past the 16-element uncomp_buf stack buffer at dims[14] = uncomp_buf[16] (mat5.c:4877), reproducing the described stack buffer over-read when reading the rank and dimensions of a compressed MAT variable.
